explanation.rationale: Atom swap to Si: adds 1 structural alert (heavy_metal); logP -1.7, SA score +0.7, Fsp3 -0.04. Why: Silicon is a carbon isostere that tends to raise lipophilicity; exploratory, seldom used in practice.
Atom swap to F: SA score +0.6, Fsp3 -0.04, logP -0.3. Why: Fluorine terminates a position, often blocks oxidative metabolism and tends to modestly raise lipophilicity.

Add I atom: adds 3 structural alerts (alkyl_halide, iodine, primary_halide_sulfate); MW +126 Da, QED -0.16, rotatable bonds +1. Why: Adding iodine usually raises MW and logP substantially and is rarely desirable in leads.
Add sulfonamide: TPSA +60 Å², logP -1.6, MW +79 Da. Why: A sulfonamide is a polar donor/acceptor group that tends to lower logP and raise TPSA.
Add N atom: TPSA +26 Å², logP -1.1, HBD +1. Why: Adding nitrogen tends to add polarity and a hydrogen-bond donor/acceptor.
Add carboxamide: TPSA +43 Å², HBD +1, logP -1.0. Why: A primary amide adds donor and acceptor, tending to lower logP and raise TPSA.

Atom swap to S: adds 1 structural alert (thiol_2); SA score +1.4, HBD +1, QED -0.05. Why: Sulfur is larger and more lipophilic than oxygen; swapping it in tends to raise logP and can add a metabolic soft spot.
Add amino: TPSA +26 Å², logP -1.1, HBD +1. Why: Adding NH2 generally lowers logP, raises TPSA and may add a basic centre.
Add methylsulfone: TPSA +34 Å², MW +78 Da, HBA +2. Why: A methylsulfone is a polar, metabolically stable acceptor that tends to lower logP and raise TPSA.

Atom swap to I: adds 4 structural alerts (alkyl_halide, iodine, alpha_halo_carbonyl, secondary_halide_sulfate); MW +112 Da, QED -0.14, SA score +0.6. Why: Iodine is heavy and lipophilic; usually raises MW and logP substantially and is rarely desirable in leads.
BRICS crossover: logP +1.7, MW +76 Da, Fsp3 -0.14.
Add acetyl: rotatable bonds +2, TPSA +17 Å², MW +42 Da. Why: An acetyl group adds a hydrogen-bond acceptor and tends to lower logP slightly.
BRICS crossover: TPSA +34 Å², MW +78 Da, HBA +2.

Change bond order to single: adds 2 structural alerts (het-C-het_not_in_ring, non_ring_acetal); HBD +1, Fsp3 +0.08, QED -0.08. Why: Reducing a multiple bond to single saturates the link and tends to raise Fsp3 and conformational flexibility.
Add methyl: TPSA -14 Å², rotatable bonds +1, Fsp3 +0.04. Why: Adding a methyl tends to raise logP slightly and can fill a pocket or block metabolism.
Atom swap to N: HBD +1, TPSA +12 Å², HBA +1. Why: Swapping in nitrogen tends to add a hydrogen-bond donor/acceptor and polarity, and can introduce a basic centre.
Add carboxamide: TPSA +43 Å², QED -0.12, logP -1.1. Why: A primary amide adds donor and acceptor, tending to lower logP and raise TPSA.
BRICS crossover: logP +1.7, MW +76 Da, Fsp3 -0.15.

Atom swap to O: adds 1 structural alert (alpha_halo_heteroatom); Fsp3 -0.05, HBA +1, TPSA +9 Å². Why: Oxygen is a hydrogen-bond acceptor; the swap tends to lower logP and raise TPSA relative to carbon.
Add methylsulfone: TPSA +34 Å², MW +78 Da, QED -0.13. Why: A methylsulfone is a polar, metabolically stable acceptor that tends to lower logP and raise TPSA.
Add S atom: adds 1 structural alert (thiol_2); QED -0.17, HBD +1, MW +32 Da. Why: Adding sulfur tends to raise lipophilicity and MW and can add a metabolic soft spot.
Add halogen (Cl): adds 1 structural alert (halogen_heteroatom); HBD -1, MW +34 Da, logP +0.6. Why: Adding chlorine tends to raise logP and can block a metabolic site.
Add F atom: SA score +0.7, rotatable bonds +1, MW +18 Da. Why: Adding fluorine (where valence allows) often blocks metabolism and modestly raises lipophilicity.
Atom swap to F: Fsp3 -0.05, SA score +0.3, logP -0.1. Why: Fluorine terminates a position, often blocks oxidative metabolism and tends to modestly raise lipophilicity.
